Test exposure associations with donor-level cell composition

Source: R/composition.R
run_exposure_composition.Rd

Tests whether an exposure is associated with the joint cell-composition profile while retaining donors, rather than cells or repeated biological samples, as the independent units of inference.

Usage

run_exposure_composition(
  x,
  exposure,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  replicate_col = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  min_cells = 10L,
  support_min_donors = 10L,
  support_min_total_cells = 100L,
  celltype_universe = NULL,
  exclude_celltypes = character(),
  zero_prior = 0.5,
  replicate_aggregation = c("equal_replicate", "pooled_counts"),
  n_permutations = 0L,
  permutation_strata = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x).

exposure

Character scalar naming the exposure variable.

celltype_col

Character scalar naming the cell-type column in colData(x).

replicate_col

Optional character scalar naming biological samples nested within donors. If NULL, each donor is treated as one sample.

covariates

Character vector naming numeric design columns in exposureData(x).

min_cells

Minimum number of cells from the retained universe per biological sample.

support_min_donors

Minimum number of donors in which a cell type must be observed. Support is evaluated without reference to exposure values.

support_min_total_cells

Minimum total number of cells required for a cell type, also evaluated without reference to exposure values.

celltype_universe

Optional pre-specified character vector of cell types eligible for analysis.

exclude_celltypes

Character vector of annotation labels excluded before support filtering.

zero_prior

Positive symmetric Dirichlet prior. The default 0.5 is the Jeffreys prior.

replicate_aggregation

Either "equal_replicate", the primary approach that averages log-ratio coordinates across samples within each donor, or "pooled_counts", which pools cells within donor and is intended as a sensitivity analysis.

n_permutations

Number of Freedman–Lane residual permutations for the omnibus test. Zero reports the asymptotic partial Pillai test only.

permutation_strata

Optional exchangeability strata for permutation. Supply a named vector indexed by donor ID for study-stratified inference.

seed

NULL (default) or a single integer, used only for permutation. With NULL the permutations draw from the caller's random-number stream, so set.seed() before the call makes them reproducible. With an integer, that seed is used inside the call and the caller's random-number state is restored before return.

Value

A DataFrame with one HC3-adjusted cell-type-versus-rest log-ratio contrast per supported cell type. metadata(result) stores the partial Pillai omnibus test, support audit, design diagnostics, and the donor-level model matrices used for inference. padj is the Holm family-wise adjusted p-value; padj_bh is supplied as a secondary false-discovery-rate summary.

Details

Counts are formed for every biological sample by supported cell type. Zeros are handled through posterior expected log proportions under a symmetric Dirichlet(1/2) prior. Orthonormal isometric log-ratio coordinates define a basis-invariant partial Pillai omnibus test. Repeated samples are averaged within donor in log-ratio space, giving every donor equal regression weight. Cell-type contrasts are exposure coefficients for log2(cell type / geometric mean of all other supported types) with HC3 heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors. Nominal 95 percent confidence intervals and Bonferroni simultaneous 95 percent family-wise intervals are both returned and labelled explicitly.

The method estimates relative composition within the supported, retained cell-type universe. It does not identify absolute cell abundance, and the Dirichlet prior handles observed zeros but does not model dissociation, capture, annotation, or tissue-sampling selection mechanisms.

Relation to other methods. speckle::propeller() (Phipson et al. 2022) transforms the cell-type proportions of each sample (logit or arcsine square root) and fits a limma linear model for each cell type to compare groups of samples. crumblr::crumblr() (Hoffman and Roussos 2026) returns centred log-ratio transformed counts with observation-level precision weights for weighted linear or linear mixed models. sccomp (Mangiola et al. 2023) fits a Bayesian beta-binomial model of composition and variability. voomCLR (Assefa et al. 2026), distributed outside Bioconductor, applies the centred log-ratio transform with observation-level variances from a voom-type mean-variance trend and offers a bias correction of the fitted coefficients. run_exposure_composition() differs from these in three respects: by default (replicate_aggregation = "equal_replicate") repeated samples of a donor are averaged in log-ratio space, so that each donor carries equal weight; the omnibus test of the whole composition uses orthonormal isometric log-ratio coordinates and does not depend on which basis is chosen; and the permutation test can be restricted to exchangeability strata such as studies (permutation_strata). Its per-cell-type contrasts use HC3 standard errors, without precision weights or empirical Bayes moderation of the variances.

References

Aitchison J (1986). The Statistical Analysis of Compositional Data. Chapman and Hall.

Freedman D, Lane D (1983). A nonstochastic interpretation of reported significance levels. Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, 1, 292–298.

Phipson B, Sim CB, Porrello ER, Hewitt AW, Powell J, Oshlack A (2022). propeller: testing for differences in cell type proportions in single cell data. Bioinformatics 38(20):4720–4726. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btac582

Hoffman GE, Roussos P (2026). Fast, flexible analysis of differences in cellular composition with crumblr. Nat Commun 17:9598. doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75681-7

Mangiola S, Roth-Schulze AJ, Trussart M, et al. (2023). sccomp: robust differential composition and variability analysis for single-cell data. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 120(33):e2203828120. doi:10.1073/pnas.2203828120

Assefa AT, Verbist B, Van den Berge K (2026). Assessing differential cell composition in single-cell studies using voomCLR. Bioinformatics 42(1):btaf637. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf637

Examples

library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(S4Vectors)
set.seed(1)
donors <- paste0("D", seq_len(12))
donor_type_counts <- t(rmultinom(
    length(donors),
    size = 30,
    prob = c(A = 0.3, B = 0.4, C = 0.3)
))
rownames(donor_type_counts) <- donors
cell_donor <- rep(donors, each = 30)
cell_type <- unlist(
    lapply(seq_along(donors), function(i) {
        rep(colnames(donor_type_counts), donor_type_counts[i, ])
    }),
    use.names = FALSE
)
counts <- matrix(rpois(20 * length(cell_donor), 5), nrow = 20,
    dimnames = list(paste0("G", seq_len(20)),
        paste0("c", seq_along(cell_donor))))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = DataFrame(
        cell_id = colnames(counts),
        donor_id = cell_donor,
        cell_type = cell_type))
exp_mat <- cbind(X1 = rep(0:1, 6), age = seq(40, 62, by = 2))
rownames(exp_mat) <- donors
scee <- build_scee(sce, exp_mat, sample_col = "donor_id")
run_exposure_composition(
    scee,
    exposure = "X1",
    covariates = "age",
    min_cells = 10L,
    support_min_donors = 3L,
    support_min_total_cells = 10L
)
